quests.hint: 'Having worked' begins the sentence as a reason.
quests.explanation: 'Having + past participle' shows an earlier experience that explains the main clause.
quests.textToSpeak: Having worked in customer service for several years, she's very good at staying calm under pressure.
quests.correctAnswer: Having worked in customer service for several years, she's very good at staying calm under pressure.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Several' /ˈsevrəl/ is often two or three syllables. 'Pressure' /ˈpreʃə/ has /ʃ/. 'Staying' starts with /st/. 'Calm' /kɑːm/ has a silent 'l'.

quests.hint: 'Used to getting' is different from 'used to get'.
quests.explanation: 'Be used to + -ing' means being accustomed to something, unlike the past habit 'used to + verb'.
quests.textToSpeak: Being the youngest in the family, he was used to getting away with things.
quests.correctAnswer: Being the youngest in the family, he was used to getting away with things.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Used to' /juːst tə/. 'Getting away' links: ge-ting-a-way. 'Youngest' /ˈjʌŋɡɪst/ has /ŋɡ/.

quests.explanation: 'Not having' works as a subject, and 'saves us a lot of' gives the practical benefit.
quests.textToSpeak: Not having a car makes life more complicated, but it saves us a lot of money.
quests.correctAnswer: Not having a car makes life more complicated, but it saves us a lot of money.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Complicated' /ˈkɒmplɪkeɪtɪd/ has four syllables. 'Saves us' links: say-vzus. 'A lot of' links: ə-lo-təv.

quests.explanation: 'We'd be happy to' is a polite business phrase, and 'as long as' sets a condition.
quests.textToSpeak: We'd be happy to consider a longer contract, as long as the terms stay flexible.
quests.correctAnswer: We'd be happy to consider a longer contract, as long as the terms stay flexible.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Contract' as a noun is /ˈkɒntrækt/, stressed on CON. 'Flexible' /ˈfleksəbl/. 'Terms' /tɜːmz/ ends in /mz/.

quests.hint: 'I see your point' softens the disagreement.
quests.explanation: Acknowledging first, then presenting a constraint, keeps a negotiation polite.
quests.textToSpeak: I see your point, but from our side it would be difficult to commit without more information.
quests.correctAnswer: I see your point, but from our side it would be difficult to commit without more information.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Commit' /kəˈmɪt/ is stressed on MIT. 'Difficult' /ˈdɪfɪkəlt/. 'Information' /ˌɪnfəˈmeɪʃn/. 'Without' has a voiced /ð/ or voiceless /θ/, and both are common.

quests.explanation: 'Be open to + -ing' invites flexibility, and 'room for a discount' asks for a price reduction politely.
quests.textToSpeak: Would you be open to splitting the cost, or is there any room for a discount?
quests.correctAnswer: Would you be open to splitting the cost, or is there any room for a discount?
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Splitting' /ˈsplɪtɪŋ/ starts with /spl/. 'Discount' as a noun is stressed on DIS. Rise on 'cost', fall on 'discount'.

quests.explanation: 'Recommend + -ing' is the pattern, and 'although' introduces an exception.
quests.textToSpeak: Doctors generally recommend getting at least seven hours of sleep, although some people function well on less.
quests.correctAnswer: Doctors generally recommend getting at least seven hours of sleep, although some people function well on less.

quests.explanation: 'Ever since' plus a past event describes a change that has continued until now.
quests.textToSpeak: Ever since I started walking to work, I've noticed that I feel more awake in the mornings.
quests.correctAnswer: Ever since I started walking to work, I've noticed that I feel more awake in the mornings.

quests.hint: 'Motivated' is stressed on the first syllable.
quests.explanation: 'Longer than you'd expect' is a natural way to say things take more time than planned.
quests.textToSpeak: It's hard to stay motivated when you're not seeing results, but progress usually takes longer than you'd expect.
quests.correctAnswer: It's hard to stay motivated when you're not seeing results, but progress usually takes longer than you'd expect.

quests.hint: 'I'll believe it when I see it' is a fixed saying.
quests.explanation: This idiom expresses doubt about a promise.
quests.textToSpeak: The landlord says he'll fix the heating by Friday, but I'll believe it when I see it.
quests.correctAnswer: The landlord says he'll fix the heating by Friday, but I'll believe it when I see it.

quests.explanation: 'How close it is to' keeps statement order after 'how close'.
quests.textToSpeak: If you're thinking of renting there, you'll need to check how close it is to public transport.
quests.correctAnswer: If you're thinking of renting there, you'll need to check how close it is to public transport.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Renting' /ˈrentɪŋ/. 'Transport' as a noun is /ˈtrænspɔːt/. 'Public' /ˈpʌblɪk/. 'Close' here is /kləʊs/ with an /s/.

quests.explanation: The auxiliary 'do' adds emphasis to a small complaint.
quests.textToSpeak: Our neighbours are lovely, although they do tend to play music quite late on weeknights.
quests.correctAnswer: Our neighbours are lovely, although they do tend to play music quite late on weeknights.

quests.explanation: 'Make it' means be able to come, and 'it'd be great if you could' is a warm invitation.
quests.textToSpeak: We're organizing a small get-together on Saturday, so it'd be great if you could make it.
quests.correctAnswer: We're organizing a small get-together on Saturday, so it'd be great if you could make it.

quests.explanation: Thanking first, then giving a reason, is the polite structure for declining.
quests.textToSpeak: Thanks so much for the invitation, but I've already promised to help a friend move that day.
quests.correctAnswer: Thanks so much for the invitation, but I've already promised to help a friend move that day.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Invitation' /ˌɪnvɪˈteɪʃn/ is stressed on TAY. 'Promised' /ˈprɒmɪst/ ends in /st/. 'Already' /ɔːlˈredi/.

quests.explanation: 'Both into' shows shared interests, and 'neither of you knows' introduces the reason to meet.
quests.textToSpeak: You two should definitely meet, since you're both into hiking and neither of you knows anyone here.
quests.correctAnswer: You two should definitely meet, since you're both into hiking and neither of you knows anyone here.

quests.hint: 'Signing' has a silent 'g' in the spelling.
quests.explanation: 'Before + -ing' gives advice about timing, and 'small print' means the details that are easy to miss.
quests.textToSpeak: Before signing anything, read the small print carefully, because some contracts include fees that aren't obvious.
quests.correctAnswer: Before signing anything, read the small print carefully, because some contracts include fees that aren't obvious.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Signing' /ˈsaɪnɪŋ/. 'Carefully' /ˈkeəfəli/. 'Obvious' /ˈɒbviəs/. 'Contracts' as a noun is stressed on CON.

quests.explanation: Comparing prices is only useful when the real total is considered, and 'only… if' expresses that condition.
quests.textToSpeak: Comparing prices online only helps if you also factor in delivery costs and returns policies.
quests.correctAnswer: Comparing prices online only helps if you also factor in delivery costs and returns policies.

quests.explanation: The passive 'was declined' focuses on what happened to the card, and 'even though' expresses surprise.
quests.textToSpeak: The card was declined even though I'm certain there was enough money in the account.
quests.correctAnswer: The card was declined even though I'm certain there was enough money in the account.

quests.hint: 'The more… the less…' has a matching rhythm.
quests.explanation: This structure shows two things changing together.
quests.textToSpeak: The more I practice speaking, the less nervous I feel, although I still make plenty of mistakes.
quests.correctAnswer: The more I practice speaking, the less nervous I feel, although I still make plenty of mistakes.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Practice' as a verb is /ˈpræktɪs/. 'Mistakes' /mɪˈsteɪks/ ends in /ks/. 'Nervous' /ˈnɜːvəs/. 'Plenty of' links.

quests.explanation: 'Encourage someone to + verb' is the pattern, and 'how much we'd improved' uses the past perfect.
quests.textToSpeak: Our teacher encouraged us to keep a journal, so we could see how much we'd improved over time.
quests.correctAnswer: Our teacher encouraged us to keep a journal, so we could see how much we'd improved over time.

quests.explanation: 'Isn't the same as' contrasts two skills, and 'it took me years to' explains the time needed.
quests.textToSpeak: It took me years to realize that understanding a language isn't the same as speaking it.
quests.correctAnswer: It took me years to realize that understanding a language isn't the same as speaking it.

quests.explanation: 'Leaning towards' shows a preference that isn't final, and 'flexibility' is the reason.
quests.textToSpeak: We're leaning towards the second option, mainly because it gives us more flexibility if plans change.
quests.correctAnswer: We're leaning towards the second option, mainly because it gives us more flexibility if plans change.

quests.hint: 'Hold off on' means wait before doing.
quests.explanation: 'Hold off on + -ing' is a practical way to say 'wait', and 'for sure' means definitely.
quests.textToSpeak: Let's hold off on booking anything until we know for sure whether Priya can join us.
quests.correctAnswer: Let's hold off on booking anything until we know for sure whether Priya can join us.

quests.explanation: 'Once' plus present perfect passive sets a condition for starting, and 'get… moving' means make progress.
quests.textToSpeak: Once the budget's been approved, we can start hiring and get the whole thing moving.
quests.correctAnswer: Once the budget's been approved, we can start hiring and get the whole thing moving.

quests.explanation: Naming two causes with 'partly… and partly…' is a neat way to explain a situation.
quests.textToSpeak: The reason it's so expensive is partly because the materials are imported and partly because demand is high.
quests.correctAnswer: The reason it's so expensive is partly because the materials are imported and partly because demand is high.

quests.explanation: 'What surprised me most was that…' is a strong way to introduce an unexpected fact.
quests.textToSpeak: What surprised me most was that hardly anyone in the room had actually read the report.
quests.correctAnswer: What surprised me most was that hardly anyone in the room had actually read the report.

quests.explanation: 'Between X and Y' contrasts two ideas, and 'confuse the two' points back to both.
quests.textToSpeak: There's a big difference between being busy and being productive, and many of us confuse the two.
quests.correctAnswer: There's a big difference between being busy and being productive, and many of us confuse the two.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Difference' /ˈdɪfrəns/ is often said in two syllables. 'Confuse' /kənˈfjuːz/ ends in /z/. 'Productive' /prəˈdʌktɪv/.

quests.explanation: 'Unless' sets the exception, and 'should be able to' expresses a confident plan.
quests.textToSpeak: Unless something unexpected comes up, I should be able to send you the revised draft by tomorrow morning.
quests.correctAnswer: Unless something unexpected comes up, I should be able to send you the revised draft by tomorrow morning.

quests.explanation: 'If the weather's as bad as…' compares reality to a forecast, and 'might have to' shows possibility.
quests.textToSpeak: If the weather's as bad as they're predicting, we might have to reconsider the whole trip.
quests.correctAnswer: If the weather's as bad as they're predicting, we might have to reconsider the whole trip.

quests.hint: Say 'I'd have' as one quick unit.
quests.explanation: 'I'd have said' is 'I would have said', which describes something you didn't do, and 'but' gives the reason.
quests.textToSpeak: I'd have said something at the time, but I didn't want to embarrass anyone.
quests.correctAnswer: I'd have said something at the time, but I didn't want to embarrass anyone.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Embarrass' /ɪmˈbærəs/ is stressed on BAR. 'Something' /ˈsʌmθɪŋ/. 'Didn't want' has a light /t/.
